chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdill, from Ibn Sinan, from 'Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man wears a single garment up to his chest, he may pray in it.

He said: And I read in a letter of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), asking him about the fennec fox [skin], whether one may pray in it, so he wrote: There is no problem with it.
And I wrote asking him about the skins of rabbits, so he (peace be upon him) wrote: It is disliked.
And I wrote asking him about a garment lined with silk, whether one may pray in it, so he wrote: There is no problem with it.
ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on praying in different animal skins and silk-lined garments according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details specific jurisprudential rulings on the permissibility of praying in various garments, emphasizing that a single garment reaching the chest is sufficient for prayer. It distinguishes between materials, noting that while fennec fox skin and silk-lined garments are permissible, rabbit skin is considered disliked (makruh). These rulings reflect the practical application of purity and modesty principles in Shia fiqh, derived from the Imams' responses to specific material inquiries.
